title: Extending compact symplectic-submanifold deformations by ambient symplectic isotopies

difficulty_reason: After the expressly admitted smooth ambient isotopy extension and smooth parameter dependence of the scalar corrections, the full problem still proves the relative geometric compatibility step. An arbitrary Moser primitive gives an ambient vector field that need not be tangent to Sigma0. The author constructs a global function with prescribed differential on the symplectic normal bundle using the exponential/tubular chart, the invertible zero-section derivative, a fiberwise-linear function and a cutoff. Subtracting its exact differential preserves d(alpha_t)=-dot(omega_t) while killing the normal component, so the corresponding Moser field is tangent and its flow preserves Sigma0. The pullback/flow calculation then produces the desired ambient symplectic isotopy. This compatibility construction and complete relative-Moser chain are carried in the selected proof, rather than assumed as the target theorem. The elementary orthogonality step(b) is not separately counted; no H3 claim is proposed. Root confirms H2 for the complete Q4(a-d) after actual source-page review and focused comparison with existing selected Moser claims.

standard_prerequisites: Symplectic nondegeneracy and the tangent/symplectic-normal direct sum
Cartan formula, pullback differentiation and flows of smooth time-dependent vector fields on compact manifolds
Exponential maps, inverse function theorem, ordinary compact tubular-neighborhood shrinking and smooth cutoff functions
source_caveats: The original theorem assumes both the ambient symplectic manifoldM and all symplectic submanifoldsSigma_t compact, with a smooth familyt in[0,1]. Preserve these hypotheses; do not generalize to a noncompact ambient space or strengthen the conclusion to Hamiltonian isotopy.

The two explicitly admitted results are the ordinary smooth ambient-isotopy extension and the smooth parameter choice of the functions from(c). They remain prerequisites and are not counted as newly proved here.

Solution(a) physicalp2 calls dot(omega_t) an exact1-form, although its displayed identity dot(omega_t)=d(phi_t^*(i_Yt omega)) has degree2 and the next line correctly uses a1-formalpha_t with d(alpha_t)=-dot(omega_t). Retain the printed degree-word error; the actual differential equations are unchanged.

In(c), the solution passes from the invertible zero-section derivative of the exponential chart to a diffeomorphism on a neighborhood of the zero section. This uses the usual compact tubular-neighborhood shrinking, a standard differential-topology step, not an additional relative-Moser theorem.
The selected solution starts on physicalp2 below the end of Q3(b); full original pages keep that neighboring text, but Q3 flux/Hamiltonian material is not counted or required as a proof input for Q4.
